interaction.prompt: Your winger has the puck on the strong-side wall. Drag your three teammates into a scoring structure: a body at the net, a weak-side option, and a point to keep it in.

feedback.right: That's a scoring triangle: a net-front presence for tips and rebounds, a weak-side option for the cross-ice play, and a point to keep pucks in and shoot.
feedback.wrong: With no net-front and no weak-side option, the puck-carrier has nowhere dangerous to go. Fill the net-front, the weak side, and the point.

tip: In the offensive zone, get a body to the net, an option on the weak side, and a point to hold the line.
why: Offensive-zone structure spreads the defence: a net-front screen, a weak-side threat, and a point shooter force the defenders to cover the whole zone.
